description: VB.NET source (.vb files) targeting .NET Framework 4.x migration to C# 13 + .NET 10 LTS. Calibrated against DDI Inform (#2 in the Tier-1 portfolio). VB.NET → C# translation is lower-risk than VB6 → C# (no COM, no On Error Resume Next) but has its own idiom gap: Modules vs static classes, implicit narrowing conversions, Dim x = ... type inference vs var, With...End With blocks, string comparison operators (= vs String.Compare), late binding via Object, optional parameters with IsNothing checks, My.Settings access, and On Error GoTo (structured vs unstructured).

claimKinds.label: Invariant
claimKinds.description: Behavioural invariants the method/module must preserve across all valid inputs.

claimKinds.label: Module → static class
claimKinds.description: VB.NET Module declarations expose all members without qualification (similar to C# static imports). In C# they become static classes. Key risks: extension methods defined in a Module must become extension methods in a static class (this keyword); members accessed without qualification in other VB.NET files become fully-qualified in C#; Module-level state becomes static fields and thread-safety must be assessed.

fields.name: has_state
fields.doc: Whether the Module contains mutable Shared/static fields — if yes, thread-safety of the static class must be assessed.

fields.name: extension_methods
fields.doc: Names of any VB.NET extension methods in the Module — these must use `this` parameter in C#.

claimKinds.label: Implicit conversion risk
claimKinds.description: VB.NET with Option Strict Off allows implicit narrowing conversions that would be compiler errors in C# (e.g. assigning Double to Integer, Long to Integer, Object to a typed variable). Also covers VB.NET string-to-numeric coercions (CInt('5') = 5), Integer overflow wrapping without OverflowException (unlike C# checked context), and Date/String implicit conversions in format expressions. These become explicit casts in C# and may introduce runtime failures if the coercion path was wrong.

claimKinds.label: With...End With block
claimKinds.description: VB.NET With...End With blocks allow accessing members of an object without repeating the object reference. In C# the nearest equivalent is a scoped variable (using var x = obj; x.Prop1 = ...; x.Prop2 = ...). When the With target is a value type (Structure), .NET behaviour differs: the With block operates on a COPY, not the original — mutations inside the block are lost unless the struct is assigned back. Flag every With block on a struct/value type as a potential silent mutation loss.

fields.name: csharp_pattern
fields.doc: The recommended C# pattern (e.g. 'var order = GetOrder(); order.Total = x; order.Tax = y;' for class types; 'var s = struct; s.Field = x; struct = s;' for value types).

claimKinds.label: String comparison semantics
claimKinds.description: VB.NET string equality (=) with Option Compare Text is CASE-INSENSITIVE by default — a major semantic difference from C#'s case-sensitive ==. Also covers: VB.NET Like operator (wildcard pattern) → Regex in C#, string concatenation & vs + (VB.NET & never coerces to numeric; C#'s + can), IsNothing(s) vs s Is Nothing vs String.IsNullOrEmpty(s), and VB.NET Asc/Chr functions → (int)c and (char)i in C#.

fields.name: option_compare
fields.doc: Option Compare Text = case-insensitive (default in VB6, frequent in VB.NET); Binary = case-sensitive (matches C# ==).

claimKinds.label: Error handling contract
claimKinds.description: VB.NET supports both structured (Try/Catch/Finally) and unstructured (On Error GoTo label, On Error Resume Next) error handling, sometimes mixed in the same file. C# supports only structured try/catch. Unstructured error handling must be rewritten — On Error GoTo label → try/catch with explicit state; On Error Resume Next → try/catch per statement with bool flag. Also captures VB.NET-specific Err object use (Err.Number, Err.Description).

claimKinds.label: Side effect
claimKinds.description: Externally-visible state mutations: database writes, file I/O, My.Computer.FileSystem access, My.Settings writes, network calls (WebClient, HttpWebRequest), My.Application.Log writes, Windows Registry via My.Computer.Registry.

claimKinds.label: Edge case
claimKinds.description: Boundary and failure conditions specific to VB.NET → C# migration: Nothing vs null (VB.NET Nothing is the zero-value for value types, not null; C# null only applies to reference types and Nullable<T>), Integer division (\ vs /) operators, VB.NET Integer type is 32-bit (same as C# int), but Long is 64-bit — same name means same type, VB.NET Date serial number arithmetic, BitAnd/BitOr vs & / | in numeric context, UInteger/UShort/ULong (unsigned) in VB.NET → uint/ushort/ulong in C#.

claimKinds.label: Open question
claimKinds.description: Ambiguities that require SME resolution. Common VB.NET cases: Option Strict Off usage (late binding, implicit conversions — hard to mechanically translate), My namespace accesses (My.Settings, My.Resources, My.Forms — must decide on .NET 10 equivalents), RaiseEvent in classes (must become C# events), Inherits from Microsoft.VisualBasic.* base classes (no direct equivalent in .NET 10), XML Literals (VB.NET built-in XML syntax has no C# equivalent — must become LINQ to XML calls).

topLevelFields.name: enclosing_type
topLevelFields.doc: Module, Class, Interface, or Structure name (e.g. 'modOrders', 'clsCustomer', 'OrderService').

topLevelFields.name: option_strict
topLevelFields.doc: Option Strict setting in the file. Off = implicit conversions allowed; On = explicit only; NotDeclared = project default (usually Off for legacy VB.NET).

ioFieldShape.directionDescription: VB.NET parameter modes. ByVal = pass by value; ByRef = pass by reference; Optional = optional with default; ParamArray = variadic tail; return = function return value.

promptHints.emphasis: Check the file's Option Strict and Option Compare declarations — if absent, assume Off/Text (the permissive defaults). Every Module declaration is a moduleToStaticClass claim. Every With block is a withBlockUsage claim (especially value-type targets). Every = operator on String with Option Compare Text is a stringComparisonSemantics claim. Every implicit narrowing (Object/Double/Long assigned to Integer/String without CType/DirectCast) is an implicitConversionRisk. On Error GoTo or On Error Resume Next is an errorHandlingContract — VB.NET structured Try/Catch is fine, unstructured is not. My.Settings, My.Computer, My.Application accesses should be raised as openQuestion (no direct .NET 10 equivalent).

calibratedAgainst: DDI Inform (#2, Tier-1 portfolio Phase 12.0) — VB.NET + UniverseDB
